summary: Draft against an indexed row subset of the existing output head while verifying with the full head; greedy output unchanged
implementation_scope: Python frequency-based or ID-prefix subset choice, index/token mapping, first-maximum gather argmax, coverage, expected tokens and draft-head cost; size choice from measured rounds; reference CUDA gather-argmax kernel over FP32 head rows for a subset or the full head. Head encodings, subset size and draft integration are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: The draft head is a measurable share of draft cost and a modest subset of token IDs covers most of the workload's target tokens
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Drafting is dominated by other work, target tokens are spread evenly across the vocabulary, or the draft head is already cheap relative to verification
provides: Deterministic subset choice from token frequency with required tokens and lower-ID tie preference
ID-prefix prior for vocabularies without statistics, with required control tokens, and contiguous row runs readable without an index
Ascending subset index to token ID mapping and validation
Row gather of the existing head without requantization and first-maximum argmax mapped back to token IDs
Correctness argument: full-head verification keeps greedy output; the subset argmax equals the target whenever the target is inside
Draft-head cost formula, coverage bound and expected tokens per round
Reference CUDA gather-argmax kernel with optional logits, also usable as the full-head argmax
Subset size chosen from measured tokens per round and round time at each candidate size, not from coverage
engine_supplies: Head encoding and row decoder shared by draft and verification
Token frequency statistics, required tokens and the subset size for the model and workload
Draft-step integration, device subset array residency and resource accounting
Measured acceptance and round cost for the chosen size
preserve: Verification uses the full head and only the target accepts tokens
Subset rows are the model's head rows gathered byte for byte, with their scales
Rows are unique and ascending so subset index order is token ID order
Draft and target share token IDs and the first-maximum tie rule
adapt: Frequency source or ID-prefix prior, required tokens and subset size
Indexed reads versus a contiguous row copy, and fusion into the draft head kernel

code_files.purpose: Host reference subset choice, mapping, gather argmax, coverage, expected tokens, draft-head cost and measured size choice
CUDA gather-argmax launch interface over subset or full head rows
Reference one-block-per-state gather-argmax kernel with first-maximum reduction, not for performance

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library; CUDA C++20 with Core CRIT_CORE_CUDA for the device reference
requires.model: A drafter that projects through the target's output head rows (shared vocabulary), with a greedy target verifier
requires.workload: Greedy speculative decoding where a frequency-ranked subset covers most target tokens

contract.input: Token counts, subset size and required IDs; head rows with a row stride, ascending subset IDs and hidden states
contract.output: Ascending subset IDs, per-state draft token IDs mapped from subset indices and optional subset logits
contract.ownership: The engine owns head bytes, the device subset array and hidden-state buffers; the kernel borrows them on the caller stream
contract.failure: Reject empty, duplicate, unsorted or out-of-vocabulary subsets, sizes that cannot hold required tokens or exceed known tokens, invalid geometry and short row strides
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; the subset affects only proposals inside the engine draft step, and published tokens come from full-head verification

dependencies: CUDA runtime for the device reference

validation.host: Frequency choice, required tokens and ties, mapping validation, inside-subset equality with an exact tie, subset-drafted speculation equal to ordinary greedy output, cost, coverage and expected tokens; size choice from measured rounds with ties to the smaller size
validation.native: CUDA gather-argmax on a 1000-row padded FP32 head for subset sizes 1 to the full vocabulary: gathered logits bitwise equal to full-head logits, subset argmax equal to the full argmax whenever inside, first-maximum ties, FP64 dot comparison and invalid launches
validation.performance: No speed claim; acceptance and draft savings depend on the model, workload and chosen subset size
